---
title: "01 — Single resonance (SHO)"
---

The smallest complete **Pintelon–Schoukens** experiment: a simple harmonic oscillator
at 1 Hz with Q = 20. We run the whole pipeline end to end —

1. **design** an optimal periodic multisine that puts drive power where the model is
   most uncertain, and quantify the variance reduction over a flat drive;
2. **measure** the frequency-response function (FRF) *leakage-free* by injecting that
   multisine into a digital twin and taking a synchronous, integer-period DFT;
3. **fit** the plant by maximum likelihood, weighting each bin by its measured
   uncertainty.

No windowing, no spectral leakage, no ad-hoc smoothing — every step is the textbook
P&S estimator. This example is intentionally minimal (one mode, one twin, no hardware)
so the signal flow is clear before the ladder adds complexity.

```{python}
import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots

from system_ident.model import TFModel
from system_ident.fisher import parameter_covariance
from system_ident.design.pintelon import optimal_excitation
from system_ident.excitation import multisine_from_psd
from system_ident.backends.twin import TwinBackend
from system_ident.plant import SuspensionPlant
from system_ident.loop import SysIDLoop
from system_ident.estimators.gml import GMLEstimator

SKY, GOLD, GRAY = '#1F8AC0', '#C8973A', '#94A3B8'

# ── experiment geometry ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FS, NPERSEG, N_PERIODS = 32.0, 2048, 8
TOTAL = NPERSEG * N_PERIODS / FS                 # 512 s of record
FMIN, FMAX = 0.2, 8.0

# Synchronous DFT grid: the multisine lines must land exactly on these bins so
# the integer-period DFT is leakage-free.
f_all = np.fft.rfftfreq(NPERSEG, 1 / FS)
band  = (f_all >= FMIN) & (f_all <= FMAX)
freq  = f_all[band]

# ── plant and prior ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
true  = TFModel.from_resonances([(1.0, 20.0)],  gain=100.0)  # 1 Hz, Q = 20
prior = TFModel.from_resonances([(0.95, 18.0)], gain=110.0)  # 5% off f0, 10% off Q

Pyy    = np.ones_like(freq)          # white readout-noise floor
Px_tot = 1.0                         # fixed drive-power budget

# Optimal drive is designed from the *prior* — all we have before measuring.
Pxx_opt  = optimal_excitation(freq, prior, Pyy, Px_tot, n_iter=6)
Pxx_flat = np.full_like(freq, Px_tot / (freq[-1] - freq[0]))
```

## Designed excitation vs the plant

The optimal drive is the fixed point of the Pintelon–Schoukens *dispersion* function:
it pours power into the bins that carry the most Fisher information about $(f_0, Q)$ —
the resonance and its skirts — instead of spreading it flat. Same total power, sharper
parameters.

```{python}
#| label: fig-sho-excitation
#| fig-cap: "Top: the plant magnitude with its 1 Hz resonance (the prior used to design the drive is the faint dotted line). Bottom: the optimal drive concentrates power at the resonance; the flat drive spreads it uniformly. Hover to read exact values."

cov_opt  = parameter_covariance(freq, true, Pxx_opt,  Pyy, TOTAL)
cov_flat = parameter_covariance(freq, true, Pxx_flat, Pyy, TOTAL)
ratio    = np.max(np.diag(cov_flat)) / np.max(np.diag(cov_opt))

resp = np.abs(true.eval(freq))

fig = make_subplots(
    rows=2, cols=1, shared_xaxes=True,
    subplot_titles=[
        '<b>Plant magnitude</b>  |G(f)|',
        f'<b>Excitation design</b>  — {ratio:.0f}× variance reduction over flat',
    ],
    vertical_spacing=0.08,
)

fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=freq, y=resp, mode='lines',
    line=dict(color=SKY, width=2.5), name='|G(f)| — true plant',
    hovertemplate='%{x:.3f} Hz   |G| = %{y:.4f}<extra></extra>',
), row=1, col=1)

fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=freq, y=np.abs(prior.eval(freq)), mode='lines',
    line=dict(color='rgba(200,151,58,0.55)', width=1.5, dash='dot'),
    name='|G(f)| — prior (design model)',
    hovertemplate='%{x:.3f} Hz   |G_prior| = %{y:.4f}<extra></extra>',
), row=1, col=1)

# Mark resonance
f0_idx = int(np.argmax(resp))
fig.add_annotation(
    x=freq[f0_idx], y=resp[f0_idx], xref='x', yref='y',
    text='<b>f₀ = 1.0 Hz, Q = 20</b>', showarrow=True,
    arrowhead=2, arrowsize=1.1, arrowcolor='rgba(200,151,58,0.7)',
    ax=60, ay=-38, font=dict(size=11, color=GOLD, family='Outfit, sans-serif'),
    row=1, col=1,
)

fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=freq, y=np.sqrt(Pxx_opt),
    mode='lines', fill='tozeroy', fillcolor='rgba(200,151,58,0.15)',
    line=dict(color=GOLD, width=2.5), name='Optimal  (Fisher-matched)',
    hovertemplate='%{x:.3f} Hz   ASD = %{y:.4f}<extra></extra>',
), row=2, col=1)

fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=freq, y=np.sqrt(Pxx_flat),
    mode='lines', line=dict(color=GRAY, width=1.8, dash='dash'),
    name='Flat  (equal total power)',
    hovertemplate='%{x:.3f} Hz   ASD = %{y:.4f}<extra></extra>',
), row=2, col=1)

fig.update_layout(
    template='plotly_white', height=500,
    margin=dict(l=60, r=20, t=50, b=55),
    font=dict(family='Outfit, Inter, sans-serif', size=12),
    legend=dict(orientation='h', yanchor='bottom', y=1.02, xanchor='right', x=1,
                bgcolor='rgba(255,255,255,0.9)', bordercolor='#DCE5F0', borderwidth=1),
)
fig.update_yaxes(title_text='|G(f)|',         type='log', row=1, col=1, gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)')
fig.update_yaxes(title_text='Drive ASD',      type='log', row=2, col=1, gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)')
fig.update_xaxes(title_text='Frequency  [Hz]',            row=2, col=1, gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)')
fig.update_xaxes(gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)',        row=1, col=1)
fig.show()
```

## Parameter variance: same power, lower uncertainty

```{python}
print(f"Measurement time T = {TOTAL:.0f} s   ({N_PERIODS} periods of {NPERSEG} samples at {FS:.0f} Hz)")
print()
print(f"  Flat (equal power)  — max parameter variance: {np.max(np.diag(cov_flat)):.3e}")
print(f"  Optimal             — max parameter variance: {np.max(np.diag(cov_opt)):.3e}")
print(f"  Variance ratio:  {ratio:.1f}×  (optimal is {ratio:.0f}x better)")
```

::: {.callout-note}
The reduction in worst-parameter variance shown above does not require any extra
measurement time or drive power — only a smarter allocation of the *same* budget. This
is the entire promise of optimal experiment design.
:::

## Measure the FRF leakage-free

We now realise the optimal spectrum as a periodic **Schroeder multisine** — a sum of
harmonically related sinusoids whose period is exactly `NPERSEG` samples — inject it
into a digital twin of the suspension, and read back both the drive monitor and the
mirror motion. Because the drive is periodic over the analysis window, a synchronous
(integer-period) DFT of the response is leakage-free: the sharp resonance is measured
without the near-peak bias a windowed transform of a random record would smear in.

```{python}
plant = SuspensionPlant({"POS": true}, FS)
tw = TwinBackend(
    plant, {"C1:EXC": "POS"}, {"C1:RSP": "POS"},
    fs=FS, sensor_asd=5e-3,
)

drive = multisine_from_psd(Pxx_opt, FS, NPERSEG, N_PERIODS, freq, seed=0)
tw.inject("C1:EXC", drive, FS)
seg = tw.read(["C1:EXC", "C1:RSP"], TOTAL)

# Reference-based (ratio-of-averages) FRF over the excited band — the P&S path.
H, H_err, coh = SysIDLoop._estimate_tf_periodic(
    seg["C1:EXC"], seg["C1:RSP"], FS, NPERSEG, band
)
```

## Is the drive gentle? — the measurement time series

The Schroeder phasing gives the multisine a low crest factor: a smooth, bounded
waveform rather than an impulsive kick. The mirror settles into a steady bounded
oscillation — the suspension is being *coaxed*, not slammed. We plot the first ~64 s
(exactly one period of the drive).

```{python}
#| label: fig-sho-timeseries
#| fig-cap: "First ~64 s of the experiment (one full drive period). The drive (top) is a smooth, low-crest Schroeder multisine; the mirror motion (bottom) is a bounded oscillation dominated by the 1 Hz resonance. Peak drive stays well inside a safe actuator range."

t = np.arange(int(64 * FS)) / FS
fig = make_subplots(
    rows=2, cols=1, shared_xaxes=True, vertical_spacing=0.09,
    subplot_titles=['<b>Drive</b> — POS actuator (Schroeder multisine)',
                    '<b>Mirror motion</b> — response at the 1 Hz mode'],
)
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=t, y=seg['C1:EXC'][:t.size], mode='lines',
              line=dict(color=SKY, width=1.3), name='drive'), row=1, col=1)
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=t, y=seg['C1:RSP'][:t.size], mode='lines',
              line=dict(color=GOLD, width=1.5), name='mirror motion'), row=2, col=1)
fig.update_layout(template='plotly_white', height=460,
                  margin=dict(l=60, r=20, t=50, b=50),
                  font=dict(family='Outfit, Inter, sans-serif', size=12),
                  legend=dict(orientation='h', yanchor='bottom', y=1.05, xanchor='right', x=1))
fig.update_yaxes(title_text='drive [cts]', row=1, col=1, gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)')
fig.update_yaxes(title_text='motion [a.u.]', row=2, col=1, gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)')
fig.update_xaxes(title_text='time [s]', row=2, col=1, gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)')
fig.show()
```

## Fit by maximum likelihood

Starting from the (deliberately wrong) prior, `GMLEstimator` finds the transfer function
that best explains the measured FRF, weighting every bin by its own measured error bar
`H_err`. The undriven bins carry infinite error and simply drop out.

```{python}
fit = GMLEstimator().fit(freq, H, H_err, prior)

def _f0_q(model):
    p = np.roots(np.asarray(model.den, float))
    p = p[p.imag > 1e-9][0]
    w0 = abs(p)
    return w0 / (2 * np.pi), w0 / (2 * abs(p.real))

f0_t, q_t = _f0_q(true)
f0_p, q_p = _f0_q(prior)
f0_f, q_f = _f0_q(fit)

print(f"{'':>10}{'f0 [Hz]':>12}{'Q':>10}")
print(f"{'true':>10}{f0_t:>12.4f}{q_t:>10.2f}")
print(f"{'prior':>10}{f0_p:>12.4f}{q_p:>10.2f}")
print(f"{'fit':>10}{f0_f:>12.4f}{q_f:>10.2f}")
print()
print(f"recovery error:  f0 {100*abs(f0_f-f0_t)/f0_t:.2f}%   Q {100*abs(q_f-q_t)/q_t:.2f}%")
```

## Recovered vs measured vs true

```{python}
#| label: fig-sho-fit
#| fig-cap: "The leakage-free measurement (grey points, error bars from period-to-period scatter), the maximum-likelihood fit (gold dashed), and the true plant (blue). Power is concentrated at the resonance, so that is where the measurement is densest and the fit is pinned."

ex = np.isfinite(H_err)

fig2 = go.Figure()

fig2.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=freq, y=np.abs(true.eval(freq)), mode='lines',
    line=dict(color=SKY, width=2.5), name='True plant',
    hovertemplate='%{x:.3f} Hz   |G| = %{y:.4f}<extra></extra>',
))
fig2.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=freq[ex], y=np.abs(H[ex]), mode='markers',
    marker=dict(color='rgba(148,163,184,0.6)', size=4),
    error_y=dict(type='data', array=H_err[ex], visible=True,
                 color='rgba(148,163,184,0.4)', thickness=1, width=0),
    name='Measured (leakage-free FRF)',
    hovertemplate='%{x:.3f} Hz   |H| = %{y:.4f}<extra></extra>',
))
fig2.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=freq, y=np.abs(fit.eval(freq)), mode='lines',
    line=dict(color=GOLD, width=2.0, dash='dash'), name='ML fit',
    hovertemplate='%{x:.3f} Hz   |G_fit| = %{y:.4f}<extra></extra>',
))

fig2.update_layout(
    template='plotly_white', height=380,
    margin=dict(l=60, r=20, t=20, b=55),
    font=dict(family='Outfit, Inter, sans-serif', size=12),
    legend=dict(orientation='h', yanchor='bottom', y=1.02, xanchor='right', x=1,
                bgcolor='rgba(255,255,255,0.9)', bordercolor='#DCE5F0', borderwidth=1),
    xaxis=dict(title='Frequency  [Hz]', type='log', gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)'),
    yaxis=dict(title='|G(f)|', type='log', gridcolor='rgba(30,60,100,0.07)'),
)
fig2.show()
```
